conflicts.fact: Whether budding and binary fission are 'cell division'/asexual reproduction relative to mitosis
conflicts.versions: Lesson 10 says budding and binary fission are 'forms of cell division'; Lessons 6 and 5 call them asexual reproduction of a whole organism, and Lesson 8 DQB asks how they 'differ from mitosis'. Wording is inconsistent but not seriously misleading.

conflicts.fact: Stages of mitosis listed: whether interphase is a stage of mitosis
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says mitosis has four stages (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase) followed by cytokinesis; Lesson 7 observes and teaches interphase as one of five 'stages of mitosis' (jigsaw numbers 1-5 with interphase as stage 1).

conflicts.fact: Doubling time arithmetic of cell numbers
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says a bacterium dividing every 20 minutes gives 64 cells after 2 hours (6 divisions = 64, correct). Lesson 7 says 'doubling the number of cells each time' and one cell dividing every 24 hours gives 1024 after 10 days (correct). No conflict in arithmetic, but Lesson 7's Explained states food provides 'materials' while Lesson 1 Predict listed 'cells made from food' as a candidate idea; consistent.
Lessons 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10 use groups of 5-6; Lesson 4 uses 6 to 8; Lesson 9 uses groups of 4 (home) or 6-8; Lesson 8 uses 4-6. Inconsistent group-size guidance across the sequence.

conflicts.fact: Number of cells in the human body / baby mass
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 states roughly 30-40 trillion cells in the body from one fertilised egg, while other lessons say 'billions' of new cells.
